title: A Uniform for the Ledger
premise: Yara Blackwood, a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, keeps its ledgers in a port town that has never once made history — until a wounded stranger named Elias Vane arrives carrying letters in the handwriting of Captain Aldous Renn, the company's celebrated war hero, officially dead for two years. The letters prove Renn faked his death to expose the company's smuggling of armistice-breaking arms, and now both the company and the approaching peace delegation want him found first. As Yara hides Elias, deciphers the letters' cipher hidden in her own father's diving logs, and falls into a love neither can afford, she discovers history was always happening to people like her — it was simply never written down. Racing to enter the truth into the company's official ledger before the armistice is signed, Yara forces the record open at the cost of her indenture, Elias's freedom, and nearly her life, ending with her signing her own name as witness while Renn's fate remains deliberately, defiantly unwritten.
about_author: Wren Hartwell is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers in coastal archives, where she first noticed how many lives were recorded only as cargo weights. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Opening on a pearl-diving morning turned ledger afternoon, establishing her indenture, her father's drowned legacy, and her belief that history belongs to capitals and admirals. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking hunger.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses among the cargo scales, pressing a satchel of letters into her hands before the company guards arrive. She hides it on instinct she doesn't understand. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Handwriting of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, night. Comparing the letters against Captain Renn's official correspondence in the archive, she confirms the impossible: the corpse is writing. Emotional beat: vertigo as her ordered world tilts.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Elias Vane, Renn's former signalman, recovers in the cooperage loft and tells Yara why he ran: the letters name ships, dates, and buyers. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people trained not to trust.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Company factor Corvus Hale interrogates the staff about the stranger; Yara lies for the first time in her careful life and discovers lying fits disturbingly well. Emotional beat: guilt braided with exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Diver's Cipher
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Yara recognizes knot-and-depth markings from her father's diving logs repeating in the letters' margins — Renn learned the divers' secret code. The letters point to a cache. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He retrieves the cache at low tide — arms manifests proving the company armed both sides of the war — but is seen by a harbor watchman. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: The Peace Delegation Arrives
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Gun salutes, bunting, and Commissioner Adela Marsh, whose historians will write the war's official record. Hale courts her; Yara realizes whoever controls the paper controls the peace. Emotional beat: dread of being erased.

chapters.title: An Indenture Is a Kind of Chain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hale offers to buy out her contract if she surrenders the satchel — revealing he knows she has it. Emotional beat: temptation measured against self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Salt and Candlelight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A stolen evening between Yara and Elias in the loft: her father's story, his desertion, an almost-kiss interrupted by search lanterns. Emotional beat: love acknowledged precisely because time is short.

chapters.title: The Watchman's Price
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The watchman who saw him is found drowned — Hale cleaning loose threads. Elias understands they are no longer hiding evidence; they are surviving a manhunt. Emotional beat: cold terror.

chapters.title: Commissioner Marsh's Ear
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Risking everything, Yara approaches Marsh anonymously with one decoded page. Marsh is interested — and equally interested in burying scandal before the signing. Emotional beat: hope discovering bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Renn Lives
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A coded message lures them to a sea cave where Captain Aldous Renn himself waits, half-ruined, alive. His testimony completes the proof — and makes them all targets. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by mortality.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Company soldiers raid the cooperage; Elias is taken, the satchel seized — except Yara had already copied the manifests into the margins of ordinary ledgers. Emotional beat: loss sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive at Night
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, alone. She infiltrates the company archive to place the true record in the official ledger, finding Hale altering entries by candlelight. She hides and watches history being falsified in real time. Emotional beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Victors
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Yara trades herself — her testimony, her father's logs, her name — to Marsh in exchange for Elias's release and Renn's amnesty, knowing Marsh may simply use her. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Freed but hunted, Elias and Renn reach the signing hall's edge as bells ring; Hale moves to have Yara arrested before she can be sworn as witness. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Enter It Into the Record
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the signing chamber, Yara reads the manifests aloud, produces the original ledger pages, and demands entry before ink dries on the armistice. Hale's counterattack collapses when Marsh chooses the credible version of history. Emotional beat: climax — a voice becoming unerasable.

chapters.title: The Cost of Ink
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Victory's bill arrives: Renn, choosing exile over celebration, vanishes back into the sea lanes; Hale escapes prosecution through company lawyers but loses everything he controlled. Emotional beat: bitter, adult victory.

chapters.title: Free Paper
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her indenture is dissolved as part of Marsh's settlement; she holds her emancipation papers and finds they feel lighter and emptier than expected. Emotional beat: disorientation of freedom.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara and Elias's POV alternating. At the harbor, Elias must sail with the delegation's escort or be tried as a deserter; they choose each other in the only way left — a promise tied to a rendezvous date, written in the divers' cipher. Emotional beat: love against duty, honored rather than resolved.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. Months later, Yara works as an archivist-for-hire entering forgotten testimonies into public record, wearing no company uniform — only her own name signed at the foot of every page. A letter arrives in familiar handwriting. Emotional beat: earned hope, history finally happening to her, on her terms.
